uncertainties: The vowels in יֱהֹוִה are printed as in the image (hataf segol, holam, hiriq). I can't confirm the dagesh in כַבָּרָק. Accents are present but I didn't transcribe them.

blocks.text: כֵּן תָּגֵן עַל־עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁלוֹמֶךָ:

אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ תְּקַע בְּשׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל לְחֵרוּתֵנוּ וְשָׂא נֵס לְקַבֵּץ גָּלֻיּוֹתֵינוּ וְקָרֵב פְּזוּרֵינוּ מִבֵּין הַגּוֹיִם וּנְפוּצוֹתֵינוּ כַּנֵּס מִיַּרְכְּתֵי אָרֶץ וַהֲבִיאֵנוּ לְצִיּוֹן עִירְךָ בְּרִנָּה וְלִירוּשָׁלַיִם בֵּית מִקְדָּשְׁךָ בְּשִׂמְחַת עוֹלָם וְשָׁם נַעֲשֶׂה לְפָנֶיךָ אֶת קָרְבְּנוֹת חוֹבוֹתֵינוּ כְּמִצְוָה (כ״א כִּמְצֻוָּה) עָלֵינוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה עַבְדֶּךָ מִפִּי כְבוֹדֶךָ כָּאָמוּר:
uncertainties: The paragraph is indented and starts a new section.
The small parenthetical after כְּמִצְוָה is a variant reading (alternative nusach), not a Shabbat addition. Its abbreviation looks like כ״א but could be נ״א.
I read the variant word as כִּמְצֻוָּה, but the vowel under the vav could be qamats or segol.
I'm not sure whether the main word is כְּמִצְוָה.
I'm not sure whether כְבוֹדֶךָ is plene or defective (כְבֹדֶךָ).
I'm not sure whether גָּלֻיּוֹתֵינוּ is printed as גָּלֻיּוֹתֵינוּ or גָּלֻיוֹתֵינוּ.

uncertainties: There are unusual supralinear marks: a short overline above the final mem of וּבְמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם, and a cluster of three dots above the final mem of חָדְשֵׁכֶם. They look like accents (possibly a telisha or zarqa variant and a segolta) but I can't identify them with certainty.
Other accents are visible, for example a tevir or merkha under עַל and accents on וּתְקַעְתֶּם, but I didn't transcribe them.
The verse runs on to the next page with no punctuation at the end of this one.

sound of the Shofar and the mountain in smoke, the people saw and trembled and stood at a distance'. And in Thy holy words it is written saying: 'God has arisen with Teruah, the Lord with a Shofar sound'. And it is said: 'with trumpets and the Shofar sound cry out before the King, the Lord'. And it was said: 'Blow the Shofar on the new moon, when the moon is covered, on the day of our festival, for it is a statute for Israel, a judgment for the God of Jacob'. And it was said: 'Halleluyah, praise God for His holiness, praise Him for the strong firmament. Praise Him for His mighty deeds, praise Him for the abundance of His greatness. Praise Him with the Shofar blast, praise Him with zither and the harp. Praise Him with timbrel and dance, praise Him with string instruments and flutes, praise Him with the clash of cymbals, praise Him with the ring of cymbals. Let all with breath praise the Lord, Halleluyah. And through Thy servants the prophets it is written saying: 'all inhabitants of the world and dwellers on earth, when the banner is raised on the mountain shall you see and when the Shofar is blown shall you hear'. And it was said: 'And on that day the great Shofar will be blown and the wanderers in the land of Assyria and the banished in the land of Egypt shall come and prostrate themselves to the Lord on the holy mountain in Jerusalem'. And it was said: 'And the Lord will appear to them and His arrow shall go forth like lightning and the Lord God will blow the Shofar and He will walk in the whirlwinds of the south. The Lord of Hosts will protect them'. So mayest Thou protect Thy people Israel with Thy peace.
uncertainties: "instru-ments" is hyphenated across a line break in the print; I joined it as "instruments". The Psalm 150 quotation opens with ' and never closes, as printed.

blocks.text: א״וא
uncertainties: This is an abbreviation for אלהינו ואלהי אבותינו, printed in Hebrew before the English paragraph. Read right to left, the glyphs are א, ו, ״, א, though the order of the abbreviation marks is a little unclear.

blocks.text: Our God and God of our fathers, blow the great Shofar for our freedom and raise a banner for the gathering of our exiles and bring near our dispersed ones from the corners of the earth and bring us to Zion Thy city in mirth and to Jerusalem Thy sanctuary in eternal joy and there we will perform before Thee our sacrificial obligations according to the commandment given to us in Thy Torah through Thy servant Moses from the mouth of Thy glory as it is said: 'and on the day of your rejoicing and on your festivals and on your new moons, you shall blow trumpets over your whole-offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace-offerings
uncertainties: The words "of our" after "God" are smudged in the scan (something like "c.. /ne."). I inferred them from context and the Hebrew. The quotation runs on to the next page.

notes: On s216 the scripture citations follow the usual Musaf Shofarot pattern: a verse introduced by וְנֶאֱמַר, or by a phrase such as וּבְדִבְרֵי קָדְשְׁךָ or וְעַל־יְדֵי עֲבָדֶיךָ. In the print they run inline in one continuous paragraph. I split them into separate linkage and verse blocks.

The biblical verses on s216 carry cantillation. I gave the consonants and vowels but left out most accents because I couldn't place them reliably. A higher-resolution pass is needed to record the accents fully.

Neither page has rubrics, Shabbat additions, shofar sound sequences, footnotes or Hebrew-script German. The only parenthetical is the variant reading (כ״א or נ״א כִּמְצֻוָּה) in the אֱלֹהֵינוּ paragraph, which is an alternative nusach, not a condition-based addition.
The overlapping bands were reconciled so no text is duplicated. I checked the English page against the full image and band 3 only.
